issues.title: Invalid frozen-state cancellation for the last Euler step
issues.failure_explanation: For h=T/n and s in the final-step interval, scheme-interpo gives X^h_s=X^h_{τ_s^h}+b(U_{τ_s^h/h},X^h_{τ_s^h})(s-τ_s^h)+(Z_s-Z_{τ_s^h}). The true Δ62 therefore contains the gradient at X^h_s. The old replacement using Γ^h at τ_s^h and ∇pα(t-s,y-z) instead corresponds to putting X^h_{τ_s^h} in the kernel and omits both the intervening stable transition and frozen-drift displacement. No equality or inequality in the old source controls that omitted contribution; boundedness alone would lose the additional h^{β/α} needed for the stated rate.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate maj-D6-mainthm is unsupported, leaving the old proof of thm-main incomplete in the full stated stable/Hölder regime. This does not show that the theorem is false; the new version restores the same theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the scheme-side estimate of the final-step term Δ62 with an argument that retains the actual state X_s^h. Condition on the grid-time information so that both the intervening stable increment and the frozen-drift displacement remain present; split the drift into b(U,X_{τ_s^h}^h)-b(U,X_s^h) and b(U,X_s^h). Control the first part using Hölder regularity together with stable-kernel integration by parts and the required Besov duality/product estimate, and control the second by a valid cancellation at time s. Establish the resulting bound C(1+t^{-β/α})h^{(α+β-1)/α} p̄_α(t,y-x) throughout the stated α,β regime, after which the existing estimates for the other error terms and the Volterra argument yield thm-main unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old proof makes a genuinely invalid inference by replacing X_s^h with the frozen grid state inside a singular kernel, and the missing h-gain cannot be recovered by boundedness or a routine edit. The full theorem and rate can nevertheless be recovered by a contained but substantial new analysis of this one endpoint contribution, including a new Besov-space estimate. This preserves the theorem's hypotheses, conclusion, and rate without reconstructing the rest of the Duhamel decomposition or Gronwall argument, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: Wrong conditioning time in the diffusion Duhamel formula
issues.failure_explanation: The proposition claims a representation for the diffusion started from x at an arbitrary time s. As printed, however, the right-hand side uses E_{t_k,x}; k belongs to the separate Euler-grid notation and is neither quantified nor linked to s in the diffusion clause. Consequently the formula does not represent the stated transition density unless one imposes an unstated equality s=t_k. The supported formula conditions on X_s=x.
issues.overall_effect: The arbitrary-start diffusion clause of prop-main-estimates-D is malformed. Subsequent calculations specialize to s=0 and already write E_{0,x}, so no additional formal result needs to be marked as dependent on the erroneous general subscript.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In duhamel-Diff, replace E_{t_k,x} by E_{s,x} and state that this denotes conditioning on X_s=x. No other part of the proposition or subsequent argument needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The old source uniquely forces this correction: the diffusion is declared to start at the arbitrary time s, the free kernel and integration interval both use s, while k is unquantified and belongs only to the separate Euler-grid notation. An adept reader can correct the conditioning subscript directly and continue without repairing any inference or changing any mathematical guarantee.
